response.sql: WITH rep_counts AS (SELECT e.EmployeeId, e.City AS City, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Customer c JOIN Employee e ON e.EmployeeId = c.SupportRepId GROUP BY e.EmployeeId, e.City), city_avg AS (SELECT City, AVG(cnt * 1.0) AS avg_cnt FROM rep_counts GROUP BY City), total AS (SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total_cnt FROM rep_counts) SELECT r.City, SUM(r.cnt) AS total_customers, AVG(r.cnt - a.avg_cnt) AS avg_excess, AVG(r.cnt * 1.0 / t.total_cnt) AS avg_share FROM rep_counts r JOIN city_avg a ON a.City = r.City CROSS JOIN total t WHERE r.cnt > a.avg_cnt GROUP BY r.City

assumptions.assumption: Counts are grouped by rep (EmployeeId) and rep city; the city average is the average of per-rep customer counts among reps with at least one matched customer (reps with zero customers are not in the average).
Share denominator is the total number of customers matched to any rep across all cities, computed before the strictly-above-average filter.
Cities with no rep above their city average (e.g., only one rep or all tied) do not appear in the output.
